slides.title: Friends Leaderboards
slides.notes: Weekly friend ranking concept — Jinu22, Ellicake, Zoeooo049 on the podium.

slides.title: Friends Leaderboards already exist in Live Services
slides.notes: The dev-facing functionality is already there. The plan is a select set of priority cloud titles for the first test — Pictionary, Boggle, Scrabble, Netflix Star, Minigolf — so we can validate the friends value across surfaces.

slides.title: The Player Journey — Phases & Intents
slides.notes: Peruse, Prep, Play, Post Game, Play Again — all five phases called out equally, before the next slide narrows to where retention actually lives.

slides.title: The Player Journey — Retention Lives Here
slides.notes: Play Again stays white; the rest fade to grey. Leaderboards are aimed at the Post Game and Play Again phases.

slides.title: Overlay and Home Continuity
slides.notes: The existing friend list component, lightly tweaked, gets us a leaderboard today — and the same board should carry to the future Home screen or any other surface that proves effective.

slides.title: Cross Platform
slides.notes: Details Pages on tv have been identified as a surface where friends leaderboards could live — a Leaderboards row in the DP's action list opens the board, and “See all” expands it.

slides.title: What about the future of tv DP?
slides.notes: Evolved DP on tv is approaching testing, and the drawer and tab structure leaves room for more flexible content types — a board sitting beside Minigolf here.

slides.title: How could we use leaderboards to entice potential connection?
slides.notes: Show players their own score next to people they have actually played with, and make the friend request the obvious next move.

slides.title: What if I don't have friends yet?
slides.notes: Rank against all players or smaller cohorts, and let players share their position off platform to challenge friends and give them a reason to join.

slides.title: Anatomy of a leaderboard
slides.notes: Top title, boxshot, name, identity callouts, ranking, recurrence, stat used, footer context, board CTA — the parts a game dev configures.

slides.title: Three types of friend leaderboards that we will build
slides.notes: Data we have: existing per-title gameplay stats plus platform-level stats. Data we need: additional stats picked with the developer for retention and recurring play.
